script.text: Iran says it could reopen Hormuz in two days. But there is a catch.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says talks with Qatari mediators produced a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a route for about a fifth of the world's oil, within two days. Qatar had proposed five. Araghchi says it applies only if Washington accepts Tehran's conditions.

Those conditions include lifting sanctions, restoring oil waivers, releasing frozen funds, and fewer US forces in the region, Araghchi says. Security chief Mohsen Rezaei says the strait stays closed, and there are no nuclear talks, until the United States agrees.

Araghchi calls the Vance letter a positive step. Rezaei says Washington's tone has softened, but Iran has not replied. Secretary of State Rubio says President Trump has made no decision on resuming military action. Gulf states reportedly prepare for it.
Will the Strait of Hormuz reopen before December? Yes or no?

upload.title: Iran Offers to Reopen Hormuz in 2 Days. The Catch? #shorts
upload.description:
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says talks with Qatari mediators have produced a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days, shortening an earlier five-day proposal, but only if the United States meets Tehran's conditions. By his account these include lifting sanctions, restoring oil waivers, releasing frozen funds including those held in Qatar, and reducing U.S. forces in the region. Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei says Hormuz stays closed and nuclear talks will not start until Washington accepts Iran's seven conditions; he says he has read Vice President JD Vance's letter, describes a softer U.S. tone, and has not yet replied. Araghchi called the letter a positive step. Secretary of State Marco Rubio says President Trump has made no decision on resuming military action. The U.S. has not publicly responded to the two-day plan; all details of the plan come from Iranian officials.
